findings.finding: `MODEL_LADDER`'s dual role (name-to-window sizing AND escalation ordering) is not addressed by the plan's mechanism. `models_at_or_above` (sizing.py:312-320) and `largest_window_tokens` (sizing.py:137-146) both iterate `MODEL_LADDER`'s `(bare_name, window_tokens)` pairs using a `name in model` substring match. If `MODEL_LADDER` entries are replaced with class names (`trivial`/`standard`/`frontier`), these substring lookups against a resolved `provider:model` string in `cfg.model` silently fall through to the 'unknown → whole ladder' branch — meaning escalation always restarts from the cheapest rung regardless of the current model, and `largest_window_tokens` always returns the ceiling. If instead `MODEL_LADDER` is kept as bare names and `models_at_or_above` calls `resolve_model_string` per rung, the function receives an already-resolved `provider:model` (e.g. `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`) as its `model` argument (sizing.py:371: `models_at_or_above(cfg.model)`) and must REVERSE-MAP it to a class to find the start rung — a direction the plan never describes. The plan says the escalation ladder 'becomes CLASS names resolved through the same funnel' but does not specify how `MODEL_LADDER` is restructured or how `models_at_or_above` determines start-rung position when given a resolved id.
findings.location: MECHANISM section / `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:99-103`, `sizing.py:312-320`, `sizing.py:137-146`

Implementer keeps MODEL_LADDER as bare names but resolves rungs via `resolve_model_string` → `models_at_or_above` must now accept a resolved provider:model as its `model` arg and find its position, requiring a reverse-lookup that doesn't exist in the plan.
`largest_window_tokens` (not in scope) shares the same lookup pattern; if MODEL_LADDER changes format it silently returns the ceiling for all inputs, affecting P8 budget arithmetic.
